maps.for: Claude picks the wrong tool: which lever to pull first
maps.ask: Is the tool description the problem, or is something else steering the choice?
maps.when: Claude keeps calling the wrong tool, or keeps mixing up two similar tools.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Wrong tool picked across many phrasings, and the descriptions are one-liners
Thin or overlapping tool descriptions
Rewrite the descriptions: purpose, inputs, an example, when to use it, when not to, and when to use the sibling tool instead
Descriptions are already good, but the misroutes always follow certain words
Wording in the system prompt (or in examples) that ties those words to a tool
Find and rewrite that wording in terms of the customer's goal
Descriptions are detailed, but a few ambiguous edge cases still go wrong
Ambiguous cases
Add 2 to 4 targeted, contrasting examples
Descriptions are good, but one tool does several different jobs
Tool design
Split or rename it into purpose-specific tools (after the description fix, not first)
Wrong pick, but the server is third-party
Descriptions you cannot edit
Project guidance in CLAUDE.md that steers the choice
The agent answers in text when it must call a tool
Tool choice
tool_choice: "any" or a forced tool
A call must never happen without a condition, or tools must run in a fixed order
Instructions cannot guarantee it
A hook or prerequisite gate in code, or a forced tool_choice
Too many tools on one agent
Tool distribution
Give each agent the 4 to 5 tools its role needs
Results need cleaning before the model sees them
Raw tool output
PostToolUse hook
maps.rule: Descriptions are the main way Claude picks a tool, but not the only one. If you own the tool, fix a vague description first (when to use, when not to, inputs); if the descriptions are already good and misroutes follow certain words, look for those words in the system prompt.

maps.for: A tool is called with bad inputs: description, examples or a split
maps.ask: What was the model actually told about this tool and its inputs?
maps.when: The right tool is called, but with wrong inputs or a misused catch-all parameter.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Wrong inputs, and the description is one line
Description
Add the input format, examples, edge cases and boundaries
The description is full, but behaviour is still inconsistent
Needs demonstration
A few targeted examples
Good description, but a catch-all parameter is still misused, or one generic tool does several jobs
Tool design
Split into purpose-specific tools with typed inputs
Two tools have overlapping descriptions
Boundaries
State when to use each
Bad input reaches the tool, it fails vaguely, and the agent can't recover
Error response
Structured validation error: category, retryable, message
A valid empty result is confused with a failure
Error meaning
Distinguish an access failure from "no results"
Results arrive in mixed formats
Result shape
PostToolUse hook to normalise
maps.rule: A minimal description leads to bad calls, so first add input format, examples, edge cases and boundaries. When a good description still does not stop misuse of a catch-all input, split the tool into purpose-specific tools with defined inputs.

maps.for: What error to return for each kind of tool failure
maps.ask: What does the agent need to know about this failure to recover from it?
maps.when: A tool fails and the agent retries hopeless calls, gives up on recoverable ones, or can't explain what happened.
head: Kind of failure
What to return
What the agent does next
rows: Transient: a timeout or brief outage that passes on a retry
Retry with backoff inside the tool first; if it still fails, isError with a transient category, retryable true
Retries, or tells the customer to wait
Business rule or policy says no (over the refund limit, past the cut-off, card closed)
isError, business category, isRetryable: false, and a customer-friendly reason
Stops, explains, and offers the next option
Validation: bad input such as a wrong ID format
Validation category, saying what was wrong and the expected format
Fixes the input and retries
Not allowed for this user
Permission category
Escalates or explains
The lookup worked but found nothing
Success with an empty result, not an error
Reports that nothing was found
Every failure says "Operation failed", or two failure kinds return the same message
errorCategory + isRetryable + a short description
Can choose the right response instead of guessing
Raw error codes arrive in mixed formats
Normalise them in a PostToolUse hook
Reads one consistent shape
A rule the agent can check in advance
Put it in the tool description
Avoids the failing call altogether
A subagent can't recover locally
Pass the error up with partial results
The coordinator decides
maps.rule: Return the error's category and whether a retry can help; a uniform "failed" leaves the agent guessing. If two failures need different responses, they need different categories, and a business-rule failure should be marked not retryable with a sentence the agent can tell the customer.

maps.for: Telling "found nothing" apart from "could not look"
maps.ask: Did the tool look and find nothing, or could it not look at all?
maps.when: A search or lookup returns nothing, and an outage might be hiding behind the empty answer.
head: Situation
Right response
Why
rows: Genuinely nothing found
A valid empty result ([])
It is a real answer
The store is unreachable for minutes or longer, so an outage looks like 'no results'
isError with a category, transient and retryable
The caller can hold or retry later instead of trusting a false "nothing there"
Brief, intermittent blips of a few seconds
Retry locally with backoff, then return an error
Recovers without bothering the caller
Bad input from the caller
Validation error, not retryable
Retrying won't help
Policy forbids the action
Business error, not retryable, with an explanation
It needs a different path
Every failure says 'Operation failed'
Structured categories: transient, validation, business, permission
The caller can tell failures apart
A subagent fails and the whole run stops
Return partial results and error context to the coordinator
Avoids stopping everything for one failure
Claims lose their sources
Carry claim-source metadata through synthesis
Keeps provenance
maps.rule: Never let 'could not look' share a return value with 'looked and found nothing'. Return a structured, retryable error for outages and keep the empty result for a real no-match.

maps.for: What a failing subagent sends back to the coordinator
maps.ask: Can this failure be fixed locally, and if not, what does the coordinator need in order to decide?
maps.when: A subagent's tool call failed and you must decide what to retry and what to report upward.
head: What happened
Local action
What to return
rows: Transient fault (timeout, 503)
Retry with backoff
If it still fails: a structured error plus partial results
Permission or access denied
Don't retry
Category, affected items, partial results and alternatives
Bad input (validation)
Fix the input and retry
Only if it can't be fixed: the validation detail
The search succeeded and found nothing
Nothing to recover
A valid empty result, clearly not an error
Any failure
Never hide it or substitute something silently
A generic 'failed' and a fake success both block recovery
maps.rule: Retry only what can recover. Otherwise return structured error context with partial results and alternatives, and let the coordinator decide.

maps.ask: What may Claude still choose: text or a tool, which tool, or nothing at all?
maps.when: Claude replies in text when a tool call is needed, or a required first step sometimes doesn't run.
head: What you need
Setting
Why
rows: Text or a tool call; the model decides freely
"auto"
The default; it may return text
Some tool call instead of plain text; several tools are valid and Claude chooses well
"any"
Bans text but keeps the choice of tool
One specific tool must run first, every time
Forced {"type":"tool","name":…} on that first request, then back to auto
Removes the choice too; guaranteed
Structured output from one schema
A forced extraction tool
Schema-compliant output
The tool input must match the schema
Strict schema
Controls the shape, not whether a call happens
Certain tools only after a prerequisite has returned
A hook or prerequisite gate in code
Guaranteed across turns, in code
An instruction to call a tool first
Prompt guidance
Probabilistic: fine as guidance, not as a guarantee
Claude calls the wrong tool, or confuses two similar tools at random
Not a tool_choice problem: expand the descriptions with inputs, examples and boundaries
It is a selection problem; descriptions help picking but can't promise order
Recover after a bad call
A structured isError result
Recovery, not prevention
Results arrive in mixed formats
A PostToolUse hook to normalise
Different sources, one shape
maps.rule: "any" guarantees some tool call, not which one. To make one exact tool run first, force it by name on that request; descriptions improve picking but cannot promise order.

maps.for: Too many tools, or the wrong tools, on one agent
maps.ask: Is the agent confused among the right tools, or holding tools it shouldn't have?
maps.when: Tool selection gets worse as tools are added, or an agent keeps using tools outside its role.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Misroutes spread evenly and started as the tool count grew
Too many tools on one agent
Keep the frequent tools on the front-line agent and move rare tools to a specialist
Many off-role tools, and the descriptions are already good
Tool distribution
Scope the AgentDefinition's tool list to the role
Misroutes cluster between look-alike pairs, or a few tools with one-line descriptions get confused
Overlapping or thin descriptions
Expand the descriptions: inputs, examples, boundaries
A rare tool is called when it shouldn't be
Missing control
A hook to block it, if it must stay
A subagent often needs one quick lookup from another role
Strict scoping is too tight
One limited cross-role tool
A generic tool does many jobs
Tool design
Split into purpose-specific tools
Many exploratory calls just to learn what exists
No catalogue
An MCP resource
maps.rule: Too many tools on one agent degrades selection. Descriptions fix confused picks among the right tools; scoping fixes an agent holding the wrong tools.

maps.for: A subagent needs help from outside its role
maps.ask: What kind of outside help is it: a frequent simple check, or rare open-ended work?
maps.when: A subagent keeps reaching for capabilities that belong to another role in the middle of a task.
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Frequent, simple, uniform lookups, such as quick checks of one fact
A narrow cross-role tool such as verify_fact
Removes round trips without giving broad access
The needed facts are known before the subagent starts
Pass them explicitly in its prompt
No tool or round trip needed
Rare, complex questions needing several sources
Route them via the coordinator
It can delegate and sees all the results
The next step depends on other subagents' findings
The coordinator decides
Only it sees everything
Open-ended research mid-task, because off-role tools are available
Remove them from the AgentDefinition; the subagent reports gaps
Off-role tools get used and misused
Too many tools, and it picks the wrong one
Cut to the 4 to 5 tools the role needs
Tool overload
Material it retrieved itself lacks sources
Claim-source mapping, if retrieval is in its role
Provenance
It ignores a written rule
Make the boundary structural
Prompts are probabilistic
maps.rule: Scope tools to the role and route real gaps back through the coordinator, then add one narrow cross-role tool for the frequent, simple need. Complex cases stay with the coordinator.

maps.for: Controlling a risky tool: remove it, gate it, or guide it
maps.ask: Is this action forbidden, allowed with approval, allowed under a limit, or just a preference?
maps.when: An agent has a tool that could do harm, and you must decide how hard to control it.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: The action is not allowed from the agent at all
Access
Deny or remove the tool; keep the rest
The action is allowed with human approval
Gate
A PreToolUse hook that asks or blocks
The action is allowed under a threshold, such as an amount
Business rule
A hook that blocks above it and redirects
A preference, not a hard rule
Guidance
A CLAUDE.md or prompt instruction
The agent misuses tools outside its role
Tool distribution
Scope tools per role
maps.rule: Not allowed from the agent: remove the tool. Allowed with approval: a hook. A preference: an instruction.

maps.for: Reuse a community MCP server, describe conventions, or build your own
maps.ask: Does something already exist for this system, and is the gap capability or just context?
maps.when: You need to connect Claude to an outside system and must decide what to use or build.
head: Situation
Right choice
Why
rows: A standard system with maintained community servers
Use a community MCP server
Already built and maintained
Team-specific fields and conventions
Describe them in CLAUDE.md
Conventions are context, not capability
A proprietary system with no equivalent
Build a custom MCP server
Nothing to reuse
The agent must change things (comment, transition)
MCP tools
Actions need tools
The agent must browse a catalogue
MCP resources
Content to read
maps.rule: Prefer community MCP servers for standard integrations, put team conventions in CLAUDE.md, and build a custom server only when nothing exists.

maps.for: Where an MCP server's configuration lives
maps.ask: Who needs this server, and how do they get it without a secret being committed?
maps.when: You are adding an MCP server and must choose between the project file and your user file.
head: Situation
Where it goes
Why
rows: The whole team (and CI) needs it from first clone
Project .mcp.json, committed
Version control shares it with every clone
The shared server needs a secret
${VAR} expansion in .mcp.json; each person sets the variable in their environment
The file is committed; the value is not
A token written into a committed file
Nowhere
Use expansion instead
One person, a personal or experimental server
User-level ~/.claude.json
Private, not in git, and keeps trials out of everyone's tool list
One person, across many repositories
User-level ~/.claude.json
Configured once for all repositories
Only one machine (such as the CI runner) uses it
User-level ~/.claude.json, secret injected at runtime
Personal scope is enough; nothing to share
An audit needs per-person actions
Per-person tokens, not a shared one
Identity
Instructions on how to use a server
CLAUDE.md
Not configuration; no servers are registered there
A standard integration such as Jira
A community MCP server
Don't build what already exists
The agent prefers Grep over a better MCP tool
Improve the MCP tool's description
Selection follows descriptions
maps.rule: Shared servers go in the project's committed .mcp.json with secrets as ${VAR}, never as values; personal or experimental servers go in ~/.claude.json.

maps.for: A better MCP tool is ignored or missing
maps.ask: Is the MCP tool missing from Claude's list, or listed but losing to a built-in?
maps.when: Claude uses a built-in such as Grep, or says it has no such tool, when a better MCP tool should be doing the job.
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Claude says it has no such tool; the server was added mid-session
Not yet discovered
Restart so it connects
The tools are listed, but Claude picks a built-in; the MCP description is thin or vague
The description doesn't distinguish the tool
Rewrite it: capabilities, inputs, sample queries, and when to prefer it over the built-in
The description is already full, and the built-in is still chosen
Context elsewhere
Add a project instruction
You can't edit a third-party tool's description
Description out of reach
Guidance in CLAUDE.md
The competing tool has no legitimate use for this agent
Tool distribution
Remove it from the agent's tools
A tool must never be used here
Permissions
Deny it in settings
Several similar tools are confused with each other
Generic, overlapping tools
Clarify boundaries, or rename and split into purpose-specific tools
Misroutes follow specific words in requests
System-prompt wording
Rewrite that wording
The agent probes to learn what exists
No catalogue
An MCP resource
The server fails for one person only
Their environment or token
Check the exported variable
maps.rule: A tool missing after a mid-session config change means reconnect; a tool present but ignored means fix its description first, saying what it does that the built-in can't, before removing the alternatives.

maps.for: Too many exploratory calls: what the agent is missing
maps.ask: Is the agent calling tools to find out what exists, or because a tool is unclear?
maps.when: The agent makes many tool calls, probing around before it does any real work.
head: What you observe
What's missing
Fix
rows: Exploratory calls to learn what exists: a catalogue, hierarchy or schema
A content catalogue
Expose it as an MCP resource: readable content the server keeps current
The structure is small and rarely changes
A one-time statement of it
Describe it in the system prompt
The agent must find specific items by query
A search tool with a clear description
That is an action, so it needs a tool
Calls are badly formed or irrelevant, or the wrong tool is picked among similar ones
A clear description
Expand the description: inputs, examples, edge cases, boundaries
One generic tool does several jobs
Purpose-specific tools
Split and rename
Each call returns huge payloads that fill the context
Trimmed results
Trim to the relevant fields in a PostToolUse hook
Verbose discovery floods the main conversation
Isolation
An Explore subagent that returns a summary
Built-in Grep is preferred over a better MCP tool
A strong MCP tool description
Say what the MCP tool does better
maps.rule: If an agent spends tool calls learning what exists, publish that as an MCP resource: resources show content, tools act or fetch. Badly formed calls and wrong picks mean fixing descriptions.

maps.for: Which built-in tool to find and explore code
maps.ask: Are you matching names, searching contents, reading a file, or only after a conclusion?
maps.when: You need to locate files or understand code and must pick between Glob, Grep, Read and an Explore subagent.
head: What you need
Tool or approach
Why, or what to watch out for
rows: Files whose names or paths match a pattern (for example all tests)
Glob
Matches paths only, never contents; fast when naming is consistent
Every file that contains a text or name
Grep
Searches contents, so it works when names are unreliable; only as good as the text marker
What a file says
Read
Read selectively, not everything
Who calls a function, or how a value flows from an entry point, when you will fix it here
Grep for the entry point or references, then Read along the calls and imports
Incremental, one file at a time, not read-all-upfront
A broad survey where only the conclusion is wanted, or context is tight
An Explore subagent
Returns a summary and keeps noise out of the main context
A long session losing earlier findings
A scratchpad file of key findings
Context degrades over time
Change one unique snippet
Edit
A targeted change by unique match
maps.rule: Glob matches file names and paths; Grep searches inside files. Start from the entry point and Read outward, and delegate to Explore only when you want the conclusion, not the trail.

maps.for: Changing a file: Edit, replace_all, or Read and Write
maps.ask: Is the text you want to change unique in the file?
maps.when: You need to change a file, or an Edit just failed.
head: Situation
Tool
Why
rows: Small change, and the text is unique in the file
Edit
Targeted change; the rest is untouched
Match not unique, but neighbouring lines differ
Edit with old_string widened by nearby lines
The anchor was too short
Match not unique, and the copies are identical for many lines everywhere
Read the file, then Write it back changed
No unique anchor exists, so Edit can't target it
Every occurrence should change
Edit with replace_all
The intent is all copies
Text not found at all
Re-read the file, then edit
The file changed since it was read
A brand-new file, or a full rewrite
Write
Write replaces the whole file
You don't know where the text is
Grep for content, then Read
That is locating, not editing
The change belongs in the source of generated code
Edit the generator, if every output should change
You were in the wrong file
maps.rule: Edit needs a unique text match. If the match is ambiguous, widen it to something unique; only when nothing is unique, Read the file and Write it back.
